searchText: can we make a channel called "Phase 0 launch date" and then pin the only comment as "we all promise not to publicly speculate on Phase 0 launch dates, esp if we are a member of the core research team bc seeing this level of external uncertainty is understandably confusing to the Ethereum community and other observers" what do you all think of this proposal my familia is dying out here putting dates out before there is a date literally helps no one except the media who will write about it, and trolls who will shit on it. ETH2 has been delayed, and there are legitimate reasons, but some coherence would help on this front. I know I speak for a lot of people on this. I would tag justin drake but apparently he's not in here **jadler** (in reply to **<@420951281910284289>**) > I mean, maybe that's step 1? I strongly agree with Trent, I understand the importance of just "setting a date" for the sake of additional priority but it really doesn't look good when what, 3 or 4 dates arbitrary dates have been dropped publicly without consulting the teams? And all have been missed? We should at least have an official testnet running first before mentioning any dates IMO From an outsiders perspective this issue with ETH 2.0 date and timeline is starting to come across as a reflection of poor management, lack of prioritisation, lack of hunger and an inability to understand that competition exists along with a lack of courage to take risk. Unfortunately the damage has already been done over the short term. I'll reiterate time and time again. An individual stating a date publicly does not reflect the sentiment of the engineering efforts of the client teams I expect when a date is actually chosen for this to be communicated in mass by the various teams involved We of course understand that, everyone not involved just sees arguing over dates of a massive effort. Maybe all the teams and EF can privately discuss a better "range" of expectations for launch, and maintain that instead of publishing multiple dates on a public social forum As a suggestion for future releases: what about simply publishing a big checklist with all the tasks needed and update it from time to time? People need to see progress, setting a date may not be a good idea, but just saying "it will be done when it's done" doesn't help. Having a public checklist will allow to have something like "80% done" without the pressure of a date. Checklist also makes it much more productive for people to argue about the requirements (i.e. do we actually need X to ship? Should we add Y? etc.). vs. discussing whether it will be 2020 or 2021 https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-pm/issues/53 we've had one for a while
